Subject: TTFT & streaming handshake — PacePayments discovery follow-up

Hi Lisa / PacePayments infra team,

Thanks again for the call today — good to meet the team. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we keep momentum: 

Summary of what we heard from you:
- Peak concurrency: ~650 concurrent chat sessions during morning batch (08:00-10:30 PT).
- Typical sustained concurrency outside peak: 80-120 sessions.
- P95 response time target (user-perceived): TTFT <= 250 ms for short prompts (<= 64 tokens).
- Streaming preference: you plan to stream partial responses in the product feed; open to SSE or WebSocket depending on ease of integration.

Open questions / asks we committed to follow up on: 
1) Exact concurrency profile per minute for the morning peak (can you share a CSV of 5-min buckets?) — helps us size reserved capacity and batching windows.
2) Clarify whether you need guaranteed per-request first-byte SLO or aggregated P95 across requests.
3) Which fallback behavior is preferred if streaming connection drops mid-generation (resume vs restart)?

Proposed near-term next steps: 
- Lisa to share the concurrency CSV and an example payload (we'll treat those as inputs, not stored).
- Karhtik (runtime lead) to propose a TTFT/throughput pairing (batch size, batching window, concurrency target) and call out SSE vs WS tradeoffs.
- I'll put together an initial SLO proposal and estimated monthly units.

Attachments: I attached a short template you can drop the numbers into (PacePayments-concurrency-profile.csv) — feel free to redact anything sensitive.

If that sounds right, can we aim for the technical send by EOD tomorrow?

Thanks,

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: TTFT & streaming handshake — PacePayments discovery follow-up

Hi Lisa, Jordan — following up with a few technical clarifications from the runtime side so we can size correctly: 

Thanks for sharing the high-level numbers on the call. Two quick items I need to recommend a concrete profile: 

1) Burst shape and arrival distribution: is the morning peak a ramp (steady increase across 30–45 minutes) or an abrupt fan-in (many simultaneous requests at once)? A ramp lets us warm caches/kv-stores and reduces TTFT variance.

2) Max tokens per request: we saw 'short prompts' on the call, but please confirm typical generation length (median / 95th). The TTFT path changes with sequence length.

3) Streaming protocol preference: some notes on tradeoffs —
- SSE (server-sent events): simpler for web clients, automatic reconnect semantics in many libraries; slightly heavier per-connection CPU on our side for long-lived connections.
- WebSocket: lower per-connection overhead and better for high-frequency two-way interactions, but requires client-side connection handling and heartbeats.

4) Concurrency tolerance: do you require hard per-request TTFT limits (i.e., SLA that we must meet per token emission) or comfortable with tail-based SLO (P95/P99) that allows occasional outliers?

If you can drop the CSV, I'll take a look and post a proposed configuration (batch size, KV cache warmstart, expected tokens/sec per GPU) and an initial SLO draft for Jordan to bundle into the commercial ask.

For transparency: our preliminary back-of-envelope for a 650-concurrent morning peak, median length ~64 tokens, P95 TTFT <= 250 ms would likely map to a small fleet of dedicated GPUs with batching windows ~10–20 ms and prefix caching — I'll put numbers against that after I see the CSV.

Thanks — Karthik
Karthik Iyer | Runtime Lead, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: TTFT & streaming handshake — PacePayments discovery follow-up

Jordan / Karthik,

Thanks for the clear recap. Attaching the concurrency CSV (PacePayments-concurrency-profile.csv) — five-minute buckets for last 30 days; morning peak is consistently between 06:30-09:00 PT for us. A couple of answers inline below: 

- Burst shape: More of a ramp with small spikes. The ramp is steep for ~20 minutes then settles into a plateau with microbursts.
- Max tokens: median 48, 95th 210. We try to keep most prompts short; the 95th are edge-case receipts and reconciliation flows.
- Streaming protocol: SSE would be easier to drop into our web feed; mobile clients currently use a wrapper over WebSocket. If you can support both that's ideal but SSE-first is OK.
- SLO expectations: For the customer-facing UI we want a user-perceived first-token under 300 ms P95 and <500 ms P99. We understand occasional outliers are acceptable.

Fallback behavior: prefer restart on reconnect. If a stream drops, the client will request a fresh generation with the same prompt and we will deduplicate on our side if needed.

Doc links: we can't share internal traffic graphs but the CSV has the shape you asked for.

Next: please send your SLO proposal and a short note on the deployment pattern (hosted vs dedicated) and expected monthly unit estimate. Happy to review and set a technical workshop next week.

Thanks,
Lisa Grant
Head of Product — Messaging | PacePayments
lisa@pacepayments.com

Attachments: PacePayments-concurrency-profile.csv
